configs.description: The PDU as it ships: no cord, nothing seated. The two mounting ears are on it and are drawn only where a viewer asks for ears. The cable clamp and its screws are in the box and are not drawn.
configs.name: base

gaps.note: three printed widths and none is the body. Spec sheet, Unit Dimensions: 19.000 in, and 44,5 cm in the row below (19 in is 482.6 mm). Owner manual, Specifications: 17 1/4 in beside 445 mm (17.25 in is 438.2 mm). The straight-on rear photograph, scaled on the stated outlet pitch, measures the body at 434.2, and the same photograph scaled on the stated C19 spacing at 436.0. 434.2 is drawn. 19 in is read as over the ears; 17 1/4 in may be the body with the ear brackets screwed to its sides, which no source says.
gaps.wanted: a dimensional drawing of the PDU12IEC, or a rule across the body of a unit.

gaps.note: spec sheet, Unit Dimensions: 4.250 in, and 10,8 cm. Owner manual, Specifications: 3 3/4 in beside 108 mm (3.75 in is 95 mm). 108 is used: it is printed in millimetres by both documents and in inches by one. No top or side view exists to measure.
gaps.wanted: a dimensional drawing, or a rule along the side of a unit.

gaps.note: the only photograph of the front is taken from above and to one side. A projective reading puts the four outlets in the middle of the face, where they are drawn, but gives their pitch as 29.2 against the stated 28.75 and the ear span as 471 against a rack face of 482.6, so it does not close and the block may be 3 mm either way. The mark at the left end is placed by the same reading.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph of the front, or a dimensional drawing.

gaps.note: the owner manual lists two 16 A resettable breakers and the spec sheet one load bank of 14 outlets; neither says what each breaker protects. Searched: the spec sheet, the Eaton SKU export, the owner manual text and its three figures, and both 230 V brochures. No outlet states the breaker it runs through.
gaps.wanted: a wiring diagram of the PDU12IEC, or the word of the maker on what each breaker protects.

gaps.note: the owner manual (Connecting the PDU) fits a cable clamp bracket round the inlet with two chassis screws and a third that tightens on the cord. It is in no photograph, and the one figure of it is perspective line art with no dimension. It is not drawn, and neither are its screw holes.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the rear with the clamp fitted, with a scale.

gaps.note: a pale round mark 5.8 mm across sits below the grounding stud. The 3000 px photograph shows a faint figure on it and does not resolve it; the white lettering of the front mark, at the same scale in its own photograph, resolves cleanly, so the limit is the mark's contrast and not the camera. It is drawn as a plain disc.
gaps.wanted: a close photograph of the grounding stud and the mark below it.

gaps.note: the PDU also mounts vertically beside the rails, on a wall and under a counter with its ears turned a quarter, and takes the PDUSIDEBRKT toolless side bracket, sold separately. Only the 1U rack form is modelled. A 0U use needs the ear's own dimensions and where its screws sit on the body sides, which no source gives, and a part for the PDUSIDEBRKT, of which no source is held.
gaps.wanted: a drawing of the mounting ear and of the PDUSIDEBRKT, and a straight-on photograph of a side.

gaps.note: the owner manual gives the nominal voltage as 100V to 240V; the spec sheet lists input voltages from 120 to 240 and titles the unit 120-240V. Both are carried in `input-ac`. THE CURRENT AT THE LOW END DIFFERS TOO: the owner manual gives the output as 15 amps for 100V to 120V and 16 amps for 208 to 240V; the spec sheet gives 16A total at every voltage, with 1.92kW at 120V, which is 16 A. `input-current-a` is 16, the figure both give at 240 V.
gaps.wanted: the rating label of a unit.

gaps.note: no source shows the top, the bottom or a side straight on. The front and three-quarter photographs see a plain lid at a steep angle and one ear side on; the owner manual figures are perspective line art. The four faces are sized from the chassis and drawn bare.
gaps.wanted: straight-on photographs of the top, the bottom and one side, with a scale.

breakers.note: datasheet and photo - owner manual, Specifications: "Circuit Breaker(s) (Resettable): 2 x 16 amps", and Features: "When a circuit breaker trips, its plunger will pop up"; spec sheet: "Dual 16A circuit breakers" in the text and "16A circuit breaker" in the table. PDU12IEC_BK shows two round plungers in nickel hex nuts, common/breaker-push-reset@1. WHAT EACH ONE PROTECTS IS NOT STATED: the spec sheet calls the 14 outlets one load bank, so the two are not one per bank, and nothing held says whether they stand in the two conductors of the feed or split the outlets. So no outlet states `through` and no breaker states `lines` (gaps: breaker-wiring).

capability.note: datasheet - spec sheet: "PDU Type: Basic"; "Switches: No power switch"; "Switchless design prevents accidental shutdown". No meter, no display and no network interface is listed or photographed. So `metering-scope: none` and `outlet-switching: false`, the class `basic` (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 2.2), and no outlet declares a state.

chassis.note: photo-measured for the width, datasheet for the height and the weight, estimated for the depth. WIDTH: the body is 2519 px in PDU12IEC_BK, 434.2 mm at the scale under `method`. No printed figure is the body: the spec sheet gives 19.000 in beside 44,5 cm, the owner manual 17 1/4 in beside 445 mm, and the photograph of the front shows the ears standing outside the body, so 19 in is read as over the ears (gaps: body-width). HEIGHT: spec sheet 1.750 in, 1U; the photograph reads 43.8. DEPTH: 108, the spec sheet figure (4.250 in, 10,8 cm) and the millimetre figure of the owner manual, which prints 3 3/4 in beside it; 108 is printed three times and 95 implied once, and no top or side view exists to measure (gaps: depth). NOT FULL DEPTH: at 108 deep, in a rack the spec sheet asks to be at least 7.8 in (198 mm) deep, it leaves the opposite face of its rack unit free, so `full-depth: false`. Weight 3.20 lb, 1.45 kg (spec sheet). Material of construction: metal (spec sheet).

colour.note: counted, because no source states a colour. PDU12IEC_BK: of the 639572 pixels of the body 94.1 percent are darker than 70 of 255 and 0.024 percent (154 pixels, the lock washer on the stud and glints on the breakers) carry any hue. The bare face reads #2b3136 at the median (28800 pixels above the parts), the C13 mouldings #2c3237 and the C19 flanges #2d3339: body, outlets and inlet are one black. The three-quarter photograph, less brightly lit, reads #1f2023 on the same face. The breaker nuts read #938c8c and #9e9798 (nickel) and the stud nut #a6adb6 (zinc). The ears in PDU12IEC_C read #3e464e and #2c343e against a face of #464f57 and #3a434b beside them: the same black.

dcim.note: the input is the inlet, one `iec-60320-c20` power port, and each outlet an `iec-60320-c13` or `iec-60320-c19` power outlet fed by it. All three slugs were read in both targets: netbox-community/netbox netbox/dcim/choices.py at 21d9223c (PowerPortTypeChoices TYPE_IEC_C20, PowerOutletTypeChoices TYPE_IEC_C13 and TYPE_IEC_C19) and nautobot/nautobot nautobot/dcim/choices.py at 061ccd5a (the same three). The outlets are named by the `interfaces:` rules (see `numbering`). NO feed_leg IS WRITTEN: a single-phase PDU is on whatever leg its cord is on (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 5.2). No outlet description names a breaker (see `breakers`).

ears.note: NOT DRAWN: THE EARS ARE SEPARATE BRACKETS, so the face is the body and the generic ear stands for them (`chassis.ears`). The owner manual (0U Rackmount Installation, step 1) unscrews them from the sides of the unit and names their screws, #6-32 flat head, 1/4 in; PDU12IEC_C shows one at each end of the front face, each with three openings (an oval, a keyhole and an oval), spanning the height of the face. The 1U Rackmount Installation figure shows them flush with the face that carries the four outlets, held by four user-supplied rack screws: one position, flush, the default. No source dimensions an ear. THE HOUSING IS REVERSIBLE (spec sheet: "Reversible all-metal housing faces front or rear in rack"): the ears stay where they are and the unit turns, which is a rack placement turned round and not a second position or a second device. For 0U, wall and under-counter mounting the same ears are turned a quarter and screwed back on (owner manual, 0U figure); that form is not modelled, and the PDUSIDEBRKT toolless 0U bracket the spec sheet sells separately is not either (gaps: zero-u).

front.note: ESTIMATED ALONG THE FACE, because the only photograph of the front, PDU12IEC_C, is taken from above and from the left: the face is 247 px high at its left end and 215 at its right, and the four C13 wells repeat at 158.2, 154.8 and 152.5 px. Read with a one-dimensional projective map fixed by the two ends of the face (the 434.2 of `chassis`) and that taper, the four centres come out evenly spaced (29.2, 29.1, 29.2) with the middle of the block at 49.4 to 50.1 percent of the face over the range of tapers the edges allow, so THE BLOCK IS DRAWN CENTRED, 174.0 to 260.25 on the stated 28.75 pitch. Read with no correction the block would sit at 53 percent. WHAT THAT LEAVES: the corrected pitch is 29.2, 1.6 percent over the stated 28.75, and the ear span comes out 471 where a rack face is 482.6, so this photograph does not close on itself and the block may be 3 mm either way (gaps: front-block). The Visio stencil preview draws the block centred too. Each outlet has its chamfered end to the left with the earth slot left of centre (the mirror of the rear), so the part is turned 270. Down the face the wells sit at 49.6 percent, the centre line. The mark at the left end is the Eaton logotype over TRIPP LITE and SERIES in plain capitals; its extent, 11.7 to 40.4 across and 11.8 to 32.8 down, is read through the same map.

ground.note: photo-measured and datasheet - spec sheet: "Rear-panel grounding lug"; owner manual, Features: "Use this screw (located by the power strip's receptacles) to connect your power strip to ground". PDU12IEC_BK shows a threaded stud with a zinc hex nut on a toothed lock washer and a flat washer. common/ground-stud@1 is the library's part of that kind; ITS NUT IS SMALLER THAN THE ONE PHOTOGRAPHED. The part draws a nut 8.1 across the corners and 7.0 across the flats; the photographed nut reads about 9.4 across the corners (9.0 to 9.9 over its three pairs, the nut being seen a little from one side) and about 8.3 across the flats. So the drawn nut is about 1.3 short either way, a compromise of size and not of place. The pale round mark below it, 5.8 across and #afbac4, carries a faint figure the 3000 px master does not resolve; it is drawn as a plain disc and not as an earth symbol (gaps: round-mark).

inlet.note: datasheet and photo - spec sheet: "Input Connection Type IEC-320 C20"; "C20 inlet accepts user supplied input cable with C19 output connection"; cord length 0. The recess reads 29.5 by 21.5 in PDU12IEC_BK against the 29.0 by 21.0 of std/c20-inlet@1. The flange round it is the inlet moulding, drawn as decor with its two screws. A CABLE CLAMP IS NOT DRAWN: the owner manual (Connecting the PDU) screws a clamp bracket to the chassis round the inlet and tightens a third screw on the cord, but the bracket is in no photograph and its figure is perspective line art (gaps: cable-clamp).

input.note: datasheet - spec sheet INPUT: single-phase; input voltage 120; 125; 127; 200; 208; 220; 230; 240; recommended service single-phase 16/20A 120-240V; maximum input 16 A ("Agency derated to 16A continuous (North America only)"); OUTPUT 3.84kW (240V) down to 1.92kW (120V), 16A total, 16A max per C19 outlet, 12A (10A CE) max per C13 outlet; 50/60 Hz. The owner manual gives the range as 100V to 240V and the output as 15 amps for 100V to 120V or 16 amps for 208 to 240V; the low end, 100 or 120, is the two documents differing, and so is the current at the low end, 15 or 16 (gaps: input-range). `input-voltage-v` is the top of the range, the one the stated 3.84 kW belongs to, and at that end both documents give 16 A, which is `input-current-a`. NO `plug-rating-a` IS STATED: the unit has an inlet and no plug, it ships no cord, and no document held rates a plug or a cord connector. The 20 of the spec sheet's "16/20A" is the service it recommends, a branch circuit of which 16 A is the continuous share, and not a rating of anything on the unit. So the exported input says 16 A and names no plug.

lifecycle.note: searched 2026-10-12 (web, "Tripp Lite PDU12IEC discontinued OR end of life OR replacement"): distributors list the part as active and no notice names it. The Eaton SKU page was live the same day. Nothing announces an end of life.

logo.note: the front prints the Eaton logotype, which is not drawn: the area it covers is the `logo-zone` region. TRIPP LITE and SERIES below it are plain capitals and are drawn as text, in white as counted (6348 pixels of the mark brighter than 170, median #fefefe). Their place is read through the map under `front` and shares its uncertainty.

method.note: NO DRAWING EXISTS, SO EVERY POSITION IS READ OFF EATON PHOTOGRAPHS. Searched: the Tripp Lite spec sheet, the Eaton SKU export and the owner manual (933401 rev D) dimension nothing on the faces; the manual figures are perspective line art; no submittal drawing, dimensional drawing or CAD file is linked from the SKU page, and the addresses the sibling PDUs use for theirs return 404. PDU12IEC_BK (the rear) is a 3000 px master taken straight on, the body alone in frame, 2519 px wide and 254 high. THE SCALE IS SET BY A FEATURE OF STATED SIZE AND PROVED BY A SECOND. The spec sheet states the rear C13 outlets 28.75 mm apart, centre to centre; the eight wells repeat at 166.79 px (their edges, their centres and each of their three contact slots fitted separately give 166.7 to 167.0, the residuals under 1.2 px and no curvature across the row), which is 5.801 px per mm. The second quantity is the stated 55 mm between the two C19 outlets: wells, slots and flange screws read 316.8 to 319.0 px, mean 317.75, which is 54.77 mm at that scale, 0.4 percent under the stated figure. Three registry dimensions agree as well: the C19 line and neutral slots read 13.06 apart against 13.0, its earth slot 8.00 off their line against 8.0, and the C13 line and neutral slots 13.88 against 14.0. So a position on the rear is good to about 0.5 mm. PDU12IEC_C (the front) is NOT orthographic and is treated separately under `front`.

numbering.note: THE UNIT PRINTS NO OUTLET NUMBERS and no vendor document numbers them, so the names are borrowed from the NetBox community device type (netbox-community/devicetype-library, device-types/Eaton/ Tripp-Lite-PDU12IEC.yaml at ffe03790): Front 1 to 4 (C13), Rear 1 and 2 (C19), Rear 3 to 10 (C13). That file gives the order of the kinds on the rear, the C19 pair before the C13 row, which is their order from the inlet end; it gives no direction, so EACH GROUP COUNTS LEFT TO RIGHT AS SEEN FROM ITS OWN FACE: Front 1 is the left of the four seen from the front, Rear 1 the C19 next to the breakers, Rear 3 the C13 next to the C19 pair and Rear 10 the last, at the end away from the inlet.

outlets.note: datasheet and photo - spec sheet: "14 total outlets-8 rear C13, 2 rear C19 and 4 front C13-in one load bank"; "(12) C13; (2) C19"; counted the same in both photographs. std/c13-outlet@1 and std/c19-outlet@1. The wells read 22.4 by 29.8 (C13) and 35.3 by 27.1 (C19) against the parts' 22.0 by 30.4 and 35.6 by 27.7. None is switched and none has a lamp.

rear.note: photo-measured - PDU12IEC_BK, mm from the rear face's left as seen from behind, and from its top. Along one centre line, 22.3 down (the parts read 22.2 to 22.4): the C20 inlet, its recess centred 25.5 across in a raised flange 0.3 to 50.3 with a screw at 4.45 and 45.65; the two C19 outlets, centred 119.15 and 173.9 as read and drawn 119.0 and 174.0, the stated 55 apart about the same midpoint, each in a flange 53.6 by 34.0 with a screw 22.5 either side; and the eight C13 outlets, centred 216.0 and every 28.75 to 417.25 (read 215.98 to 417.31), each a snap-in moulding 28.4 by 35.2 abutting the next. The grounding stud is at (56.8, 22.8), a pale round mark 5.8 across below it at (60.0, 32.6), and the two breakers one above the other at 81.2 across, 12.5 and 31.15 down, 18.65 apart. ORIENTATION, each read off the photograph: the inlet has its earth pin at the bottom and the C19 outlets their earth slot at the bottom, so both parts are turned 180; the C13 outlets lie on their sides, chamfered end to the right with the earth slot right of centre, so the part is turned 90. The face prints no legend and no outlet number.
